name: Liu Yü-hsi
bio: Liu Yü-hsi (AD 772–842) was a T’ang official and poet, known for verses of the seasons and of the court.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Summer Dying
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.text:
Whence comes the autumn's whistling blast,
With flocks of wild geese hurrying past?
Alas, when wintry breezes burst.
The lonely traveller hears them first!

poems.title: The Odalisque
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.text:
A gaily dressed damsel steps forth from her bower,
Bewailing the fate that forbids her to roam;
In the courtyard she counts up the buds on each flower,
While a dragon-fly flutters and sits on her comb.

poems.title: The City of Stones. (Nanking)
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.translator: trans. Florence Ayscough and Amy Lowell (1921)
poems.text:
Hills surround the ancient kingdom; they never change.
The tide beats against the empty city, and silently, silently, returns.
To the East, over the Huai River--the ancient moon.
Through the long, quiet night it moves, crossing the battlemented wall.

poems.title: Blacktail Row
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Grass has run wild now by the Bridge of Red-Birds;
And swallows' wings, at sunset, in Blacktail Row
Where once they visited great homes,
Dip among doorways of the poor.

poems.title: A Spring Song
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
In gala robes she comes down from her chamber
Into her courtyard, enclosure of spring . . .
When she tries from the centre to count the flowers,
On her hairpin of jade a dragon-fly poises.

poems.title: In the Temple of the First King of Shu
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Even in this world the spirit of a hero
Lives and reigns for thousands of years.
You were the firmest of the pot's three legs;
It was you who maintained the honour of the currency;
You chose a great premier to magnify your kingdom . . .
And yet you had a son so little like his father
That girls of your country were taken captive
To dance in the palace of the King of Wêi.

poems.title: Thoughts of Old Time at West Fort Mountain
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Since Wang Chün brought his towering ships down from Yi-chou,
The royal ghost has pined in the city of Nan-king.
Ten thousand feet of iron chain were sunk here to the bottom —
And then came the flag of surrender on the Wall of Stone. . . .
Cycles of change have moved into the past,
While still this mountain dignity has commanded the cold river;
And now comes the day of the Chinese world united,
And the old forts fill with ruin and with autumn reeds.

poems.title: 秋風引 (Qiu feng yin)
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
何處秋風至，蕭蕭送雁羣。
朝來入庭樹，孤客最先聞。

poems.title: 玄都觀桃花 (Xuan dou guan tao hua)
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
紫陌紅塵拂面來，無人不道看花回。
玄都觀裏桃千樹，盡是劉郎去後栽。

poems.title: 再遊玄都觀 (Zai you xuan dou guan)
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
百畝庭中半是苔，桃花淨盡菜花開。
種桃道士歸何處，前度劉郎今又來。

poems.title: 烏衣巷 (Wu yi xiang)
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
朱雀橋邊野草花，烏衣巷口夕陽斜。
舊時王謝堂前燕，飛入尋常百姓家。

poems.title: 和樂天春詞 (He le tian chun ci)
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
新妝宜面下朱樓，深鎖春光一院愁。
行到中庭數花朵，蜻蜓飛上玉搔頭。

poems.title: 蜀先主廟 (Shu xian zhu miao)
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
天地英雄氣，千秋尚凜然。
勢分三足鼎，業復五銖錢。
得相能開國，生兒不象賢。
淒涼蜀故妓，來舞魏宮前。

poems.title: 西塞山懷古 (Xi sai shan huai gu)
poems.author: Liu Yü-hsi
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
王濬樓船下益州，金陵王氣黯然收。
千尋鐵鎖沉江底，一片降幡出石頭。
人世幾回傷往事，山形依舊枕寒流。
今逢四海爲家日，故壘蕭蕭蘆荻秋。
